entries.title: The command bar takes instructions in your words
entries.body: The command bar (Cmd or Ctrl+K) takes typed or dictated instructions: jump to the first place a word appears, look a term up in the glossary, add or remove a tag, or find a phrase. If you are signed in and nothing matches, press Enter and the AI picks the nearest command from your sentence; anything that does more than move you somewhere waits for a second Enter. On your own articles, a Chat answer can end with a button that does one of these when you press it.

entries.title: Library topics follow what your articles are about
entries.body: The topics above your library can be named by the AI from each article's title and its short summary or abstract, together with your reader profile, and arranged from broad to fine. Choose a topic and its finer topics come forward; new articles are filed into the topics already there. This is built only for libraries of a moderate size. You can also sort the library by publication date, with undated articles last, and show a Published column from the Columns menu.

entries.title: The tweet thread moves into Summary
entries.body: Tweets is no longer a mode of its own: its thread is a choice in Summary, beside Brief and Fuller. Old links to the thread still open it, and typing "tweets" in the command bar finds it. The Simple level is no longer shown. Typing "rerun summary" in the command bar writes the summaries again.

entries.title: Quotes look highlighted; search hits are outlined
entries.body: In the article, a quote is marked with a purple fill, like a highlighter pen, and a search hit is marked with an outline instead. The two had been the other way round. Passages marked by Chat keep the article's own text colour, which fixes dark text that was nearly invisible on a dark background.

entries.title: Citations hide the AI's sentence unless checked
entries.body: The AI's sentence on why a cited work is relevant is hidden in the Citations list and on the card that appears when you point at a citation, unless a quick-check verdict is shown beside it. It could read as what the paper itself says. Newly built lists leave out an author or year not found in the article's text.

entries.title: Skim carries stops deeper; Referee's controls come first
entries.body: In newly planned Skim routes, a stop can be carried into the deeper passes, with small marks under its number showing which passes it is in. On a phone, Skim's arrows and depth buttons no longer close the panel. Referee's top row is its views plus a Notices button holding the confidentiality notes, and Candidates has its own search button.

entries.title: The voice is told to announce slow lookups
entries.body: In a spoken conversation, the voice is now told to say a short sentence before a slow lookup, and to ask you to repeat what it did not catch rather than guess. A call no longer ends when the AI points at a passage that is not in the article. With Experimental features switched on, the Live control offers a second voice engine to choose.

entries.title: Structure keeps your place; Profile opens tidier
entries.body: In Structure, the Fisheye list keeps every part and the sections of the part you are in, and scrolls when they do not fit, so the section you are reading no longer drops out of the list. On your profile, Account, Plan and About you start open and the other sections start shut.

entries.title: Citation line breaks and feedback screenshots fixed
entries.body: A long clause marked as a citation could be forced onto lines of its own in the article; it stays in the flow of the paragraph. In the feedback form, a screenshot containing a photograph was refused as too large; the limit is higher, and a large screenshot is scaled down to fit.
